Suotu makes a screenshot small enough to send comfortably over chat apps, while keeping the text readable.

1. Take a screenshot.
2. Open Suotu, or use Share → Suotu.
3. Optionally crop, and drag the width slider.
4. Tap Send and choose the app.

The slider sets the output WIDTH in pixels. Width matters more than a percentage: readability depends on how tall the letters end up, so a fixed percentage is too harsh for a full-screen capture and pointless for a small crop.

Measurements on rendered UI text found the readable floor is around a 10 px letter height. On a 1260-px-wide phone screenshot, small captions are about 22 px tall, which puts the safe floor near 570 px. 720 px is a comfortable default.

Quality is not a slider on purpose: the app searches for the highest quality that fits the size budget, and tests showed quality 40 and quality 90 equally readable for text while 90 cost about 70% more bytes.
Auto encodes both WebP and JPEG and keeps the better result. For screenshots WebP is usually about half the size of JPEG at the same legibility. Choose JPEG only if a recipient cannot display WebP.

Suotu can watch folders and save a small copy on its own, without opening the app. Turn it on in Settings.

Detection is event-based: the system wakes the app when the gallery changes, so nothing runs in the background while you are idle.

Copies go to the Suotu album and originals are never touched. Tapping the notification opens the share sheet directly.

Folders to watch is used for silent background shrinking. Keep it narrow — every matching file is shrunk without asking, which is rarely what you want for camera photos.

Folders to offer is used when you open the app, to load your newest image. This one can be broader, because nothing is saved until you tap Send.

Each rule is a folder plus a file-name pattern. Use Choose to pick a folder and Test to see which file names the pattern matches.
Nothing leaves your phone. All resizing happens on the device, there is no network access, and photo permission is only needed for folder watching and for opening your newest image.

Some chat apps re-compress images when sending unless you pick the original-quality option. The savings here are your storage and upload data, plus a predictable result. Send as a file to keep the exact bytes.
Shrink screenshots for sharing, while keeping the text readable.
Built with Kotlin and Jetpack Compose. Image encoding uses the Android platform WebP and JPEG encoders; no third-party image libraries.
This app requests no network permission.
